Admissible explicitly includes actual differentiability, L-smoothness, global lower bound, supplied initial-gap upper bound, existing IID and unbiased finite-variance oracle conditions, and exact event-oracle equality. No minimizer, convexity, workerwise divergence or trajectory-derived tuning parameter is added.

The actual expressions use R=max1 natCeil(sigma^2/eps), blocks=natCeil(48LDelta/eps), and natural K=R*blocks. The clock deadline divides each work function by four before roundTime takes floor increments. Accuracy is expected squared gradient <=eps, preserving the source tolerance.

allowedAlgorithm pins ringmaster q exactly. Output is its selected point paired with its actual last-update clock, a necessary pair for the source time claim. The algorithm observes event replies; it has no hidden objective or computation-power access and receives only derived tuning.

The explicit marginal and tape ProbabilityMeasures are connected by the existing IID structure; the exact stochastic-gradient provider has unbiasedness and centered second-moment bound. Success uses its supplied output law explicitly, with measurable output and integrable squared gradient. There is no hidden MeasureSpace or expected helper.

This setup exports no public theorem and appropriately has no catalog result row yet. It defines a nonconditional finite-domain accuracy/time criterion on one named output. The later Convergence witness must establish both components for the same event execution and derived natural budget.

The source time headline remains ENNReal deadline, while the actual returned clock is real and enters through ofReal. Natural K is a distinct count of event calls/updates. Because allowedAlgorithm fixes the genuine factory, the time criterion cannot be satisfied by inventing an arbitrary negative clock.
